# Brahmadattattheragāthā (Thag 6.12)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

 Cross-tradition parallels are documented in the *Krodhavarga* ("Chapter on Anger") of the Sanskrit and Tibetan *Udānavarga* (UV 20, UVS 20, Uv Kg 20) and related Chinese *Dharmapada* and *Udānavarga* translations (T 210.25, T 212.21, T 213.20). Resembling verses also align with verse 96 of the Pali *Dhammapada* (Dhp 96) and corresponding mind and arhat chapters in the Patna Dharmapada (P-Dhp 84–95), Udānavarga (UV 31), and Chinese parallels (T 210.15, T 212.32, T 213.31).

Automated analysis by DharmaNexus corroborates these connections, detecting extensive Pali-internal text reuse with the *Brāhmaṇa Saṁyutta* (SN 7) and *Sakka Saṁyutta* (SN 11), with segments 1.4–4.4 shared almost verbatim [DharmaNexus]. The text is also cited or reused in the *Nettippakaraṇa* (*Sāsanapaṭṭhāna*, Ne 37), the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, the commentaries to the *Itivuttaka* and *Suttanipāta*, and the *Visuddhimagga* [DharmaNexus]. In addition, DharmaNexus aligns passages with the Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 99) and *Dīrghāgama* translations (T 1, T 25) [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
